summary.text: 六 is the numeral ‘six,’ attested in oracle-bone records as a cardinal number and in a month name. Its graphic origin is disputed: proposals include a shelter picture, a conventional counting mark, or an early graph similar to 入.

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. One account treats the whole form as a pictograph of a simple shelter; other proposals treat it as a conventional counting mark or as a graph once similar to 入 and later distinguished. The Shuowen analysis through 入 and 八 in 易 numerology is a historical interpretation that the paleographic discussion considers unlikely to preserve the original graphic meaning.

history.text: The oracle-script-style and Western Zhou bronze-script-style images are modern reconstructions labeled for different script traditions. They provide examples of those styles, but do not establish a sequence of graphic changes or settle the graph’s origin.
The Shuowen explanation connects 六 with 入 and 八 through 易 numerology; this is a historical account, not a demonstrated graphic breakdown.

uncertainties.text: The graphic origin remains unresolved among proposals that 六 was once similar to 入, depicted a shelter associated with 廬, or served as a conventional counting mark. The cited numeral uses do not decide among them.

The proposed borrowing from a shelter word is unconfirmed: the shelter’s name and pronunciation are not independently established, and the cited Old Chinese reconstructions for 六 and 廬 do not substantiate a sound match.

senses.text: Cited oracle-bone records use 六 as a cardinal numeral in “six sheep” and in a month name meaning “sixth month.” They attest both uses but do not establish which came first.

limitations.text: The earliest cited evidence already uses 六 as a numeral. A prior shelter meaning and a transition from that meaning to ‘six’ are not established; the proposed sound-based borrowing remains unconfirmed.
The relative chronology of the cardinal and ordinal uses is unresolved.

relationships.text: Cited oracle-bone records use 六 as a cardinal numeral in “six sheep” and in a month name meaning “sixth month.” They attest both uses but do not establish which came first.

overview.text: 六 is a single graph meaning “six,” with no supported present-day component split. Oracle-bone records already use it as a numeral, but its original graphic explanation remains disputed.

takeaway.text: A shelter picture reused for ‘six’ because its name sounded similar is only a proposal; the shelter’s name and sound match are unconfirmed.

limitations.text: Both images are modern digital reconstructions, not photographs of inscribed artifacts. Their script-style labels do not establish the character’s origin or a specific path of graphic change.
